opportunities/selling-a-business.lead: Seller-side brokerage mandates for owners of small and medium-sized businesses: mandate, opportunity preparation, buyer identification and process coordination, within the authorised brokerage scope.
opportunities/selling-a-business.summary: Seller-side brokerage mandates for owners of small and medium-sized businesses: mandate, opportunity preparation, buyer identification and process coordination, within the authorised brokerage scope. Delivered within the approved licence scope and a written mandate. Not real estate brokerage, investment advice, capital raising, legal advice, valuation or tax advice.

pillars.title: A defined mandate
pillars.desc: What NK&CO is appointed to do, for whom and on what terms is written down before any buyer is approached.

pillars.title: Information, organised
pillars.desc: The seller supplies the information; NK&CO organises it. It is not represented as independently verified.

pillars.title: A controlled process
pillars.desc: Confidentiality, disclosure and approaches are managed in stages the seller has agreed.

challenges: An owner who has not decided what a good outcome looks like
Information scattered across people, spreadsheets and messages
Buyers approached before confidentiality is protected
Advisers working without a shared timetable
deliverables: A recorded statement of the owner’s sale objectives
A written brokerage mandate with scope, fee basis and exclusions
A factual business profile or anonymised summary
A buyer-identification strategy and enquiry register
A transaction timetable and outstanding-items list
A closure note confirming the end of the mandate
outcomes: A mandate both sides understand
Material a buyer can read in one sitting
Interested buyers recorded and followed up
An orderly process to the agreed end of the mandate

method.v: Understand the owner’s objectives and reasons for selling.
Agree the mandate, authority, fee basis and exclusions.
Organise supplied information into a profile and data-room index.
Identify buyer categories and make approaches where authorised.
Run the timetable with the parties and their advisers to the end of the mandate.

scope.d: Defining what NK&CO is appointed to do, for whom and on what terms before any buyer is approached.
Organising what the seller supplies into material a buyer can read. Transaction-support material, not verified statements.
Finding buyers whose criteria fit, and approaching them only as far as the mandate allows.
Keeping a sale organised from first meeting to completion, within the permitted role.

cases.title: Illustrative: two-branch service business
cases.body: An owner agrees a brokerage mandate, a profile is prepared from supplied records and buyers are approached in stages. Lawyers handle the legal documents.

cases.title: Illustrative: founder-led business
cases.body: A founder’s dependencies are listed before approaches begin, so buyers’ first questions are answered in advance.

cases.title: Illustrative: confidential sale
cases.body: Only an anonymised summary is circulated until a buyer has signed confidentiality terms.

faqs.a: No. A sale depends on buyers and terms outside NK&CO’s control, and NK&CO does not promise one.
NK&CO can discuss indicative pricing. A formal valuation is a separate professional service, which NK&CO coordinates through an independent valuer.
The parties’ own lawyers. NK&CO does not draft reserved legal documents.

faqs.q: Can NK&CO act for the buyer too?
faqs.a: Only after a conflict assessment, with disclosure and consent. Acting for both parties receives particular scrutiny.

pillars.title: Information, organised
pillars.desc: The seller supplies the information; NK&CO organises it. It is not represented as independently verified.

pillars.title: A controlled process
pillars.desc: Confidentiality, disclosure and approaches are managed in stages the seller has agreed.

challenges: An owner who has not decided what a good outcome looks like
Information scattered across people, spreadsheets and messages
Buyers approached before confidentiality is protected
Advisers working without a shared timetable
deliverables: A recorded statement of the owner’s sale objectives
A written brokerage mandate with scope, fee basis and exclusions
A factual business profile or anonymised summary
A buyer-identification strategy and enquiry register
A transaction timetable and outstanding-items list
A closure note confirming the end of the mandate
outcomes: A mandate both sides understand
Material a buyer can read in one sitting
Interested buyers recorded and followed up
An orderly process to the agreed end of the mandate

method.v: Understand the owner’s objectives and reasons for selling.
Agree the mandate, authority, fee basis and exclusions.
Organise supplied information into a profile and data-room index.
Identify buyer categories and make approaches where authorised.
Run the timetable with the parties and their advisers to the end of the mandate.

scope.d: A factual business description: operating history, products and services, locations, management and ownership, based on information supplied by the owner.
A short opportunity summary that does not identify the business, for use in a first approach where authorised.
Collecting and organising the financial and operational information the client supplies. NK&CO does not represent it as independently verified.
An index of documents, and lists of what a buyer is likely to ask for, so requests are handled in order.
A list of open questions for the seller’s legal, tax and accounting advisers, who deal with those matters.

cases.title: Illustrative: two-branch service business
cases.body: An owner agrees a brokerage mandate, a profile is prepared from supplied records and buyers are approached in stages. Lawyers handle the legal documents.

cases.title: Illustrative: founder-led business
cases.body: A founder’s dependencies are listed before approaches begin, so buyers’ first questions are answered in advance.

cases.title: Illustrative: confidential sale
cases.body: Only an anonymised summary is circulated until a buyer has signed confidentiality terms.

faqs.a: No. A sale depends on buyers and terms outside NK&CO’s control, and NK&CO does not promise one.
NK&CO can discuss indicative pricing. A formal valuation is a separate professional service, which NK&CO coordinates through an independent valuer.
The parties’ own lawyers. NK&CO does not draft reserved legal documents.

faqs.q: Can NK&CO act for the buyer too?
faqs.a: Only after a conflict assessment, with disclosure and consent. Acting for both parties receives particular scrutiny.

Buyers approached before confidentiality is protected
Advisers working without a shared timetable
deliverables: A recorded statement of the owner’s sale objectives
A written brokerage mandate with scope, fee basis and exclusions
A factual business profile or anonymised summary
A buyer-identification strategy and enquiry register
A transaction timetable and outstanding-items list
A closure note confirming the end of the mandate
outcomes: A mandate both sides understand
Material a buyer can read in one sitting
Interested buyers recorded and followed up
An orderly process to the agreed end of the mandate

method.v: Understand the owner’s objectives and reasons for selling.
Agree the mandate, authority, fee basis and exclusions.
Organise supplied information into a profile and data-room index.
Identify buyer categories and make approaches where authorised.
Run the timetable with the parties and their advisers to the end of the mandate.

scope.d: Strategic buyers, owner-operators, corporate acquirers and buyers in adjacent industries, compared against the business.
How buyers will be identified and in what order, agreed with the seller before approaches begin.
Introductions to prospective buyers, made only where the mandate authorises them and confidentiality is protected.
Receiving and recording non-binding expressions of interest and indicative proposals from interested parties.
A record of each buyer, enquiry, meeting and follow-up, kept for the length of the mandate.

cases.title: Illustrative: two-branch service business
cases.body: An owner agrees a brokerage mandate, a profile is prepared from supplied records and buyers are approached in stages. Lawyers handle the legal documents.

cases.title: Illustrative: founder-led business
cases.body: A founder’s dependencies are listed before approaches begin, so buyers’ first questions are answered in advance.

cases.title: Illustrative: confidential sale
cases.body: Only an anonymised summary is circulated until a buyer has signed confidentiality terms.

faqs.a: No. A sale depends on buyers and terms outside NK&CO’s control, and NK&CO does not promise one.
NK&CO can discuss indicative pricing. A formal valuation is a separate professional service, which NK&CO coordinates through an independent valuer.
The parties’ own lawyers. NK&CO does not draft reserved legal documents.

faqs.q: Can NK&CO act for the buyer too?
faqs.a: Only after a conflict assessment, with disclosure and consent. Acting for both parties receives particular scrutiny.
